claims.text: HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of 786 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a terminal strain of 13.5%.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has limited tensile ductility.
A portion of Ta will be substituted with Nb to create a series of HfZrTiTaNb alloys.
Nb incorporation will fine-tune the phase distribution.
Nb incorporation will alter grain-boundary chemistry.
Nb incorporation will produce a refined precipitate structure or secondary phases.
The Nb-induced structural changes will enhance dislocation mobility.
The Nb-induced structural changes will delay crack initiation and propagation.
Nb addition will promote more uniform deformation and alleviate strain localization.
The Nb-modified alloy will achieve at least a 20% increase in uniform elongation relative to a 13.5% baseline.
The Nb-modified alloy will retain yield strength close to 786 MPa.
The Nb-modified alloy will retain compressive strength close to 1314 MPa.
The Nb-modified alloy will retain impact-triggered energy release comparable to the baseline.
The proposed benefit is limited to Nb compositions that do not destabilize the primary phases.
The ductility improvement may not persist at very high strain rates or beyond the tested temperature range.
Quasi-static tensile testing will be conducted at an approximate strain rate of 0.001 s^-1 at room and elevated temperatures.
Matched compression and dynamic-impact tests will be used to assess retention of strength and energy release.
Failure to improve uniform elongation by at least 20% without significant losses in yield strength, compressive strength, or impact energy release will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The reported 13.5% value is identified as terminal strain, but the prediction and falsification rule use it as the baseline for uniform tensile elongation. Terminal strain and uniform elongation are not interchangeable measurements.

The intervention specifies substituting Ta with Nb, whereas the experimental design says Nb is increased while all other elements are kept constant. Ta cannot both decrease through substitution and remain constant.
